method: num_rows (exact) x mean_chars (/statistics, whole-split) x tokens/char (sampled); falls back to num_rows x sampled mean_tokens/doc when /statistics is unavailable
restored_from_run_note: This is the RESULT of the successful run for this config. A later re-run, requested to rule out rate-limit truncation, overwrote this file with a status=FAILED body (all 5 offsets HTTP 429) and then a third attempt was stopped mid-flight when the 429 quota was diagnosed as per-IP rather than per-account. The measured values below are restored verbatim from the run that completed. Nothing here is estimated after the fact.

configs.n_sampled_shortfall_cause: shared per-IP datasets-server 429 quota, NOT a corpus defect. The stats-ratio estimate does not depend on sample size for its heavy-tailed factor, so the shortfall affects only tokens_per_char (CV 0.1005 -- already tight).
configs.confidence_note: /statistics mean is PARTIAL -- it covers 1,453,000 of 97,270,686 rows, i.e. the head of the split, which biases the result if parquet row order correlates with crawl date. Cross-checked against a random-offset sample and the two independent estimators diverge only 12.5%, well under the 25% alarm threshold. tokens_per_char CV 0.1005 is tight. The card's 'around 100B gpt2 tokens' is confirmed to within 0.25%.
configs.dolma2_to_upstream_ratio_note: vs the corpus's own gpt2-based token_count column (upstream mean 1,183.86 tokens/doc). dolma2 and gpt2 agree within 0.6% on this corpus, so FineWeb-Edu's advertised counts are usable as-is -- unlike peS2o's whitespace-word counts.
configs.card_tokens_note: card: 'sample-100BT: a subset randomly sampled from the whole dataset of around 100B gpt2 tokens'. Parent corpus is 1.3T tokens.
configs.license_detail: ODC-By v1.0. cardData license: odc-by; card 'Licensing Information' names Open Data Commons Attribution License (ODC-By) v1.0. Use also subject to CommonCrawl Terms of Use. Not gated.
configs.lineage: CommonCrawl HTML. FineWeb-Edu = FineWeb filtered at educational score >= 3 by a Snowflake-arctic-embed-based classifier trained on Llama3-70B-Instruct annotations; that removed 92% of FineWeb, leaving 1.3T tokens. sample-10BT subset-of sample-100BT subset-of sample-350BT subset-of fineweb-edu(1.3T) subset-of fineweb-edu-score-2(5.4T) subset-of fineweb. NOT globally deduplicated (a dedup'd variant lives in HuggingFaceTB/smollm-corpus).
configs.optional_refinement: A parquet-footer scan (artifacts/recount/_footer_chars.py) would make the doc-length factor exact and remove the partial-mean caveat entirely. The method was calibrated on this very dataset's sample-10BT config, where footers gave 4780.4 bytes/doc against /statistics' 4746.6 chars/doc -- 0.7% agreement, in the expected direction since bytes >= chars.
